evidence.note: Checked tree-sitter availability and built an AST-inspection helper at the outset — a build-vs-reuse choice to leverage an existing Java parser rather than hand-roll recursive descent. Sound foundational bet, but made up front, not as a correction to a stall.
Whole-file rewrites of folding_range.rs and semantic_tokens.rs after incremental edits failed to converge — choosing a fresh implementation over layering more patches (anchor-5 behavior).

After many failed local patches on JavaDoc hover, pivoted to a materially different tactic: generated a javadocs.rs data module and rewrote hover.rs around it, updating handlers.rs. Reworking a design choice for that method with dependent updates (touches anchor 8).

Dominant mode is hundreds of small local edits to semantic.rs (the resolution engine) — case-by-case fixes for overloads, records, enums, references. No root-cause rearchitecture of the symbol/resolution model, which keeps the level below 8.
Consistent test→inspect-failing-file→edit→rebuild loop with fresh targeted investigation per failure; never repeats the same failed edit, ruling out the 0-3 band.

reasoning: The agent made a sound up-front build-vs-reuse choice (tree-sitter parser) and, when specific pieces stalled, repeatedly switched to materially different tactics — whole-handler rewrites (semantic_tokens, folding) and a hover→generated-javadocs-module pivot with dependent handler updates — which exceeds anchor 5 and brushes anchor 8. But the bulk of the resolution work (semantic.rs) was carried by incremental local patching rather than a deliberate foundational rearchitecture, and the strongest foundational choice was made at the start rather than as falsification-driven correction, so it does not reach the decisive, repeated root-cause reworking of 8-10. This lands at a 6.
